fibre_center.note: centre of the wool bundle on the distaff (drafting reference)

grip.note: attachment point: spindle = top of the yarn leader (the pinch); distaff = where the left fist closes round the stick. Prop root = hold * inverse(grip)

models.role: small wicker basket (0.30 m) heaped with raw undyed wool; base centre at the origin

pick_point.note: top of the wool heap in the basket

models.role: PERSON-001 r002 body/rig/skin/palette unchanged + in-place clips spin_enter, spin_stand, spin_exit, spin_walk + distaff_hold (hand.L) and animated spindle_hold (hand.R)

distaff_hold.note: NEW, static child of bone hand.L: attach distaff_with_fibre so that its grip coincides with this node (stick passes through the left fist)

carry_anchor.note: unchanged PERSON-001 r002 node under hand.R (not used by these clips)

spindle_hold.note: NEW, child of bone hand.R, ANIMATED in every clip (translation+rotation tracks): stays at the right thumb/index pinch, keeps the hung spindle plumb (quasi-static pendulum lean <= 9 deg) and spins it about its axis in spin_stand/spin_walk. Attach spindle_whorl so that its grip coincides with this node
spindle_hold.local_trs_note: node rest TRS = its spin_stand t=0 value; animated per frame in every clip

reference_ids: MC11 (content/research/next-batch/references/MC11-spindle-whorls-prague.jpg; Zde, CC BY-SA 4.0; City of Prague Museum whorls 'Neolithic to Bronze Age'): general biconical/drum whorl form only, viewed, not incorporated
KY16 Kyselý 2016, Živa 2016/5 p. 227 via content/research/economy/subsistence.md (sheep/wool regionally; spinnable wool in Europe from the 3rd millennium BCE)
content/research/economy/crafts-exchange.md §2.3 (flax not in the Březnice crop list, E-negative), §F7 (spinning while walking between tasks, R)
parts_and_uncertainties: E (general, not local): ceramic spindle whorls are generic across Bohemian prehistory (MC11); no Březnice whorl verified.
E (regional): wool from sheep (KY16 p. 227); flax absent from the Březnice crop list (E-negative) -> fibre is shown as undyed wool, type R.
R: whorl size (~42 mm), biconical form and low position on the shaft; shaft length/diameter; cop shape; yarn leader.

R: distaff length, forked/plain top, fibre bundle shape; held in the left fist, lower end towards the left hip (the 'under left arm' of the brief is interpreted as held in the crook of the left forearm).
R: basket form, wool colours (cream and natural brown), ball/skein forms.
R: spinning posture, drafting cycle, wrist flick, spindle spin rate (4 turns per 2 s standing, 2 per 1 s walking: slowed for 30 fps readability, real spindles turn faster), plumb-line lean.
F: who spins, where and when (demo placement).

deviations: Two extra one-shot clips spin_enter/spin_exit (1 s each) start/end exactly on the r002 idle t=0 pose; the brief's loops spin_stand (2 s) and spin_walk (1 s) loop on the spinning pose / a walking phase, as in WORK-001 (grind_enter/grind/grind_exit) and GATHER-001 (basket_walk).

spindle_hold is an animated node (translation + rotation keys in every clip) rather than a static anchor, so the attached spindle hangs plumb, follows the pinch and spins; Godot imports these as position/rotation tracks on Skeleton3D/hand_R/spindle_hold.
The drafted fibre strand between the distaff bundle and the right pinch is not modelled (it would need a stretching mesh; invisible at village scale).

In spin_enter t=0 / spin_exit end (= r002 idle) the distaff is carried horizontally in the relaxed left hand and the spindle hangs beside the right leg; game code may instead hide the props outside the spin clips.
Inspection uses this job's own tools (source/inspect_glb.py etc.), not tools/inspect_asset.py, which does not know batch-5 IDs.
